## 2. Document Characterizations

| Dimension | Finding | Evidence |
|-----------|---------|----------|
| **Legal form** | Executive agreement (Acuerdo); secondary legislation under pre-existing Decretos, not a new law | C-01, C-02 |
| **Issuing authority** | SHCP's Unidad de Política de Ingresos no Tributarios, via a named individual (Ramírez Arras); not a cabinet-level or presidential decree | C-01, C-09 |
| **Emergency vs. standing** | Appears standing/recurring — weekly stimulus schedule under 2016 and 2022框架; this specific period is routine biweekly publication | C-02, C-03 |
| **Targeting** | Stimulus is price-based (IEPS reduction), therefore automatically applied at pump; no individual eligibility screening. Lower-octane gasoline (伤民/省油) receives support; premium gasoline and non-fossil fuels receive none | C-04, C-05 |
| **Funding mechanism** | Tax expenditure (IEPS quota reduction), not cash outlay; no disclosed offsetting revenue or spending cuts in this document | C-06 (implicit) |
| **Mandatory vs. discretionary language** | "dan a conocer" (notify) — the agreement is a notification/_tblication of rates already established by Decree; "shall" (procedente) not applicable as the rates are mechanically derived | C-01, C-10 |
| **Sunset/review mechanism** | Not addressed in extract; rates are published weekly and presumed valid only for the declared period | C-03 |
| **Monitoring/reporting** | No monitoring, audit, or disclosure requirements in this document; rates are published in DOF | Not present in extract |

---

## 3. Source Incentives and Limitations

**Source incentives:**
- SHCP is both the implementing agency and the publishing authority; incentive to present rates as technical/administrative rather than political
- The agreement uses formulaic, mechanical language ("se dan a conocer") to frame rates as notifications rather than discretionary decisions

**Limitations of this document:**
1. **No stated policy rationale** — the extract contains no preamble explaining *why* the stimulus is being maintained, adjusted, or targeted to specific fuels for this period
2. **No distributional analysis** — no official estimates of受益 household count, regional distribution, or inflation effect
3. **No fiscal cost figure** — the aggregate budgetary cost of the stimulus for this period is not computed or disclosed
4. **No eligibility screening evidence** — the mechanism is price-based; no data on whether intended beneficiaries (lower-income households) actually consume more regular gasoline vs. transport/logistics diesel users
5. **No implementationlag disclosure** — whether rates were actually passed through to pump prices is not addressed
6. **No comparison to prior periods** — no context on whether 26.96% / 59.77% represent increases, decreases, or maintenance relative to prior weeks
7. **Partial legal basis** — references two Decretos but the full text of those Decretos (which establish the legal framework) is not included here; this agreement is subordinate/derivative

---

## 4. Sections a Stronger Model Should Reopen

1. **Preambular language** — the extract begins mid-sentence ("correspondien"); the stated rationale for this specific period's stimulus levels is missing. A stronger model should request the full DOF publication to capture any stated policy purpose
2. **Fuel-price pass-through** — this document does not establish whether the IEPS reduction was actually reflected in pump prices; verify against CRE (energy regulator) price bulletins for Dec 10–16 2022
3. **Aggregate fiscal cost** — the document publishes per-liter rates but not total revenue forgone; cross-reference SHCP's monthly fiscal cost disclosures for IEPS stimulus line
4. **Distributional evidence** — who consumes regular vs. premium gasoline in Mexico is empirically contested; the premise that this subsidizes lower-income households is asserted nowhere in this document
5. **Prior-period comparison** — whether this stimulus level represents a change from prior weeks (indicating a shock response under 5B.9) requires the preceding 2–4 weekly agreements for context
6. **Political context** — December 2022 was post-election (June 2022 midterms); the timing of sustained fuel subsidies near year-end requires cross-checking against political calendar for patronage interpretation (5B.1, 5B.6)
7. **Amendment history** — the extract references "posteriores modificaciones" to the 2016 Decree; whether the stimulus formula itself was changed between 2016 and December 2022 affects whether this is the same policy or a modified one
